lectures.abstract: Collider events are naturally unordered, variable-cardinality sets of detector hits or particle-flow candidates living on irregular geometries—not regular 2D pixel grids. This lecture develops geometric deep learning architectures engineered for HEP: permutation-invariant Deep Sets and infrared-and- collinear-safe Energy Flow Networks ( EFN / PFN ), dynamic latent-space distance-weighted graph networks ( GravNet and GarNet ) for irregular calorimeter clustering, dynamic graph CNNs ( EdgeConv / ParticleNet ) operating on particle clouds, and the Particle Transformer ( ParT ), which injects physically motivated pairwise interaction features (ln ∆R, ln k T , ln z, ln m 2 ) as pre-softmax attention biases. We conclude with Lorentz-equivariant networks ( LorentzNet ) and state-of-the-art FCC-ee multi-class jet flavour tagging (b, c, s, u, d, g).

deliverables.lectureNote: Formal proof of permutation invariance/equivariance and IRC safety in EFNs; exact layer equations for GravNet distance-weighted message passing, ParticleNet EdgeConv blocks, and ParT Pairwise Multi-Head Attention ( P-MHA ) + Class Attention; computational complexity (O(N 2 ) vs. O(N k)) and memory-scaling comparisons.
deliverables.lab: Stage 1 implements a lightweight PFN and EdgeConv layer from scratch in PyTorch on synthetic 2-prong vs. 1-prong particle clouds; Stage 2 trains and compares ParticleNet and ParT (with pairwise kinematic interaction biases) on a JetClass or FCC-ee flavour-tagging subset, evaluating s-tagging and c-tagging background rejection curves.
deliverables.problemSet: Analytical proof that EFN is strictly IRC-safe while PFN breaks IRC safety via non-linear z i dependence; derivation of ParT ’s four pairwise kinematic variables and their boost invariance; computational profiling of FLOPs, parameter count, and tagging rejection comparing PFN , ParticleNet , and ParT ; exit criterion: demonstrating ParT outperforming PFN by > 2× in background rejection at 50% signal efficiency on benchmark jets.
deliverables.readingListStructure: Core spine: Qasim et al. (2019) GravNet / GarNet , Qu & Gouskos (2020) ParticleNet , and Qu, Li & Qian (2022) ParT ; advanced progression: Komiske, Metodiev & Thaler (2019) EFN / PFN , Gong et al. (2022) LorentzNet , and Bedeschi, Gouskos & Selvaggi (2022–2024) FCC-ee jet flavour tagging.

learningOutcomes: Justify why unordered particle-cloud and graph representations
outperform calorimeter-image CNNs on irregular detector geometries.
Construct permutation-invariant Deep Sets ( EFN / PFN ) and analyze the trade-off between strict IRC safety and discrimination power.

Implement dynamic k-NN message passing ( EdgeConv in ParticleNet ) and latent-space distance-weighted aggregation ( GravNet ) for reconstruction and tagging. Formulate the Particle Transformer ( ParT ) attention block incorporating
pairwise 4-momentum interaction matrices as pre-softmax biases.
Explain how group-equivariant architectures ( LorentzNet ) enforce SO + (1, 3) symmetry directly in hidden representations.
Apply multi-class jet flavour taggers (b, c, s, u, d, g) to FCC-ee physics benchmarks, incorporating V 0 and K ± /π ± PID features.

lectures.abstract: Detailed Geant4 simulation of electromagnetic and hadronic showers in high-granularity calorimeters dominates experimental computing budgets, creating an acute bottleneck for HL-LHC and FCC-ee. This lecture surveys deep generative surrogates that accelerate shower generation by 10 3 –10 5 × while preserving multi-layer energy correlations and sparsity: conditional GANs ( CaloGAN ), exact-likelihood normalizing flows ( CaloFlow and distilled CaloFlow II ), score-based diffusion models ( CaloScore , DDPM, and SDE/probability-flow ODE formulations), point-cloud diffusion ( CaloClouds ), and continuous normalizing flows via Flow Matching. We emphasize rigorous physics validation established by CaloChallenge 2022 , especially adversarial classifier metrics (AUC between Geant4 and generated showers) and energy-conservation checks.

deliverables.lectureNote: Derivations of the change-of-variables Jacobian determinant in coupling/autoregressive normalizing flows, denoising score matching and reverse-time SDEs/probability-flow ODEs, optimal-transport conditional Flow Matching, and the CaloChallenge evaluation protocol (1D marginals, shower-shape moments, and binary-classifier fidelity test).
deliverables.lab: Stage 1 builds a conditional RealNVP normalizing flow and a toy 1D/2D DDPM in PyTorch on synthetic longitudinal shower profiles; Stage 2 trains a conditional normalizing flow or score-based model on CaloChallenge Dataset 1 (photons), measures generation time per shower vs. Geant4 , and computes the Geant4 -vs.-surrogate classifier AUC.
deliverables.problemSet: Analytical derivation of the forward/reverse KL divergence behavior explaining GAN mode collapse vs. flow mode covering; derivation of the probability-flow ODE from the variance-preserving SDE; computational trade-off study comparing sampling speed (NFE) against classifier AUC for flow, distilled flow, and diffusion models; exit criterion: trained surrogate achieving < 1 ms/shower on GPU with layer-energy mean agreement within 3% and documented classifier AUC.

Contrast voxel-grid surrogates against geometry-independent point-cloud generators ( CaloClouds ) for ultra-granular calorimeters.
Audit generative-model fidelity rigorously using physical shower-shape observables, correlation matrices, and post-hoc binary-classifier tests.

lectures.abstract: Traditional binned histogram analyses discard high-dimensional kinematic correlations and rely on explicit signal hypotheses. This lecture introduces two transformative statistical-ML paradigms for HEP. First, Simulation-Based Inference (SBI) bypasses intractable detector-level likelihoods p(x|θ) = dz p(x|z)p(z|θ) by training neural ratio estimators (NRE/CARL) and score-augmented estimators ( RASCAL / ALICES / SALLY , mining joint likelihood R ratios and scores from matrix-element simulators) to extract unbinned, high-dimensional EFT constraints. Second, model-agnostic resonant anomaly detection extends the classic bump hunt: Classification Without Labels ( CWoLa / CWoLa Hunting ) learns optimal classifiers directly from signal-region vs. sideband mixtures, while CATHODE interpolates a conditional normalizing flow across sidebands to oversample the background and neutralize feature-mass correlations.

deliverables.lectureNote: Exact derivation of the likelihood-ratio trick for NRE, the joint score t(x, z|θ) = ∇ θ ln p(x, z|θ) and why regressing on it is unbiased for the marginal score ∇ θ ln p(x|θ), the proof of CWoLa optimality under conditional independence, and the CATHODE two-stage density-interpolation + classifier algorithm.
deliverables.lab: Stage 1 builds an amortized Neural Ratio Estimator (NRE) in PyTorch for a synthetic 2-parameter SMEFT-like differential distribution with intractable detector smearing, comparing NRE contours against a 1D binned histogram fit; Stage 2 implements CWoLa Hunting and CATHODE (using a conditional normalizing flow) on a benchmark LHC Olympics 2020 resonant dijet subset, measuring significance improvement characteristic (SIC) curves.
deliverables.problemSet: Analytical proof that CWoLa fails when auxiliary features x correlate with the resonant variable m and how CATHODE resolves this; derivation of the Fisher-information saturation of SALLY near a reference point θ 0 ; computational simulation-based calibration (SBC) coverage check for NRE posteriors; exit criterion: NRE achieving strictly tighter 68% CL contours than 1D binning with calibrated coverage, and CATHODE achieving SIC max > 5 on the injected benchmark signal.

(2021) LHC Olympics 2020, and Aarrestad et al. (2022) Dark Machines Challenge.

learningOutcomes: Formulate the intractable marginal likelihood integral in collider
physics and classify SBI methods (NRE, NLE, NPE, and simulator-augmented RASCAL / ALICES ).
Prove that minimizing squared error against the latent joint score t(x, z|θ 0 ) recovers the exact marginal score ∇ θ ln p(x|θ 0 ) for locally optimal EFT inference.
Train and validate an amortized Neural Ratio Estimator using diagnostic calibration and empirical coverage checks. Prove the optimality of Classification Without Labels ( CWoLa ) for
statistical mixtures and identify its vulnerability to mass-feature correlations.
Implement CATHODE by training a conditional normalizing flow on sideband regions, interpolating into the signal window, and training a weakly supervised classifier.
Benchmark anomaly-detection algorithms using Significance Improvement Characteristic (SIC) curves while controlling false-positive rates and look-elsewhere effects.

lectures.abstract: A neural network only impacts physics when it runs reliably within the strict memory, throughput, and latency budgets of offline reconstruction frameworks or real-time hardware triggers. This lecture covers the complete deployment pipeline across two regimes. For offline reconstruction and high-level triggers (O(ms)), students export PyTorch models to ONNX , verify numerical parity, apply post-training INT8 quantization in ONNX Runtime , and examine heterogeneous coprocessor-as-a-service inference ( SONIC /Triton). For Level-1 hardware triggers (O(100 ns–5 µs)), students master fixed-point arithmetic ( ap_fixed<W,I> ), pruning, quantization-aware training (QAT with straight-through estimators and QKeras / QONNX ), and automated High-Level Synthesis ( hls4ml ) targeting FPGA DSP, LUT, and BRAM resource ceilings with controlled initiation intervals.

deliverables.lectureNote: Exact specification of affine/symmetric integer quantization and fixed-point ap_fixed<W,I> dynamic-range bounds; straight-through estimator (STE) gradient derivation for QAT; FPGA resource-latency Pareto modeling ( ReuseFactor , Initiation Interval II , DSP/LUT/BRAM scaling); ONNX operator-graph optimization and SONIC client-server architecture.
deliverables.lab: Stage 1 exports a trained PyTorch jet classifier to ONNX , validates <1e-5 FP32 parity in ONNX Runtime , applies static INT8 quantization, and profiles CPU latency/throughput; Stage 2 trains a pruned, quantized compact jet tagger via QAT, converts it through hls4ml ( QONNX or QKeras frontend), runs C-simulation verifying bit-accurate agreement, and inspects estimated FPGA latency (clock cycles) and DSP/LUT utilization.
deliverables.problemSet: Analytical calculation of bit-width ap_fixed<W,I> required to prevent overflow/underflow given layer weight and activation ranges; computation of minimum ReuseFactor to fit an N × M matrix-vector multiply within a fixed DSP budget while meeting an II ≤ 4 clock-cycle target at 200 MHz; computational accuracy-vs.-bitwidth Pareto sweep (FP32, 16-bit, 8-bit, 4-bit) in hls4ml ; exit criterion: < 1% AUC degradation at ≤ 8-bit fixed-point precision with simulated FPGA latency < 1 µs.

(2018) integer quantization, and ONNX Runtime quantization docs; advanced progression: Aarrestad et al. (2021) FPGA CNNs, Iiyama et al. (2021) FPGA GNNs, Krupa et al. (2021) SONIC GPU-as-a-service, and 2025 hls4ml platform paper.

parts.abstract: Part 13 synthesizes the entire ComPart curriculum into the experimental landscape of the Future Circular Collider (FCC) integrated programme housed in a 90.7 km underground tunnel at CERN. Beginning from the flagship physics benchmarks of the electron-positron Higgs, electroweak, and top factory (FCC-ee) and the subsequent 100 TeV proton-proton collider (FCC-hh), this module maps target precisions onto concrete detector performance requirements. Students systematically dissect the three leading FCC-ee detector concepts—CLD, IDEA, and ALLEGRO—alongside the FCC-hh reference detector, perform quantitative requirements-to-design trade-off studies, and culminate in three production-grade capstone projects built on Key4hep, k4geo , FCCAnalyses , and pyhf .

deliverables.lectureNote: Comprehensive graduate monograph (~180 pages across Lectures 13.1–13.7) unifying natural units (ℏ = c = 1, energies in GeV/TeV, luminosities in cm −2 s −1 and ab −1 ) with SI instrumentation quantities (µm, ps, T, X 0 , λ I , n eq cm −2 ). Includes end-to-end derivations of recoil-mass kinematics, Gluckstern momentum resolution, dual-readout compensation, noble-liquid drift √ currents, pileup energy density scaling, and √ Pareto detector optimization, with worked numerical benchmarks for every FCC-ee working point ( s = 91.2, 161, 240, 365 GeV) and FCC-hh ( s = 100 TeV).
deliverables.lab: Progressive two-stage laboratory sequence spanning all seven lectures: Stage 1 builds transparent, vectorized Python/NumPy/SciPy/PyTorch prototypes (toy recoil-mass fitter, Gluckstern tracker optimizer, dual-readout S/C compensator, LAr signal-shaping simulator, PUPPI/SoftKiller pileup filter, Pareto trade-off explorer, and toy Particle Flow engine); Stage 2 transitions directly into the production Key4hep stack ( DD4hep / k4geo geometries for CLD, IDEA, and ALLEGRO, EDM4hep , PandoraPFA , Delphes , FCCAnalyses , and pyhf ).
deliverables.problemSet: Seven integrated analytical and computational problem sets (4–5 multi-part problems each) culminating in a defended capstone portfolio. Exit criterion: reproduce published FCC Feasibility Study benchmark sensitivities within 15%, pass automated EDM4hep /schema validation on all Stage 2 pipelines, and deliver a complete pyhf profile-likelihood limit and CLD Particle Flow performance audit.
deliverables.readingListStructure: Core spine anchored on the four-volume 2019 FCC Conceptual Design Report (CDR), the 2025 FCC Feasibility Study Report (FSR), and the primary concept papers for CLD, IDEA, ALLEGRO, and FCC-hh; advanced/optional tier covering ECFA Detector R&D Roadmap DRD collaborations, Snowmass 2021 syntheses, machine-learned Particle Flow (MLPF/Transformers), and 4D timing detectors.

Quantify radiation damage (NIEL/TID), trigger rates, and extreme pileup (⟨µ⟩ ∼ 1000) at the 100 TeV FCC-hh and design 4D timing plus constituent-level mitigation strategies.

lectures.abstract: This lecture establishes the physics-driven requirements matrix for the FCC integrated programme. Starting from the four-stage FCC-ee operation plan— √ Tera-Z at s = 91.2 GeV (∼ 6 × 10 12 Z bosons across 4 IPs), W W threshold at 161 GeV, Higgsstrahlung peak at 240 GeV (10.8 ab −1 , ∼ 2.2 × 10 6 ZH events), and tt̄ threshold at 365 GeV—we derive how sub-per-mille electroweak observables, 4 MeV Higgs mass precision, and heavy-flavour/τ benchmarks dictate exact targets on momentum resolution, impact-parameter resolution, hadronic jet energy resolution, particle identification, and luminosity monitoring. We conclude by contrasting these precision lepton-collider drivers with the discovery and Higgs self-coupling (λ HHH ) demands of the 100 TeV FCC-hh.

deliverables.lectureNote: Detailed derivations of (a) the model-independent ZH recoil-mass formula m 2 sE ℓℓ + m 2 ℓℓ and error propagation from = s − 2 recoil √ √ 2 beam energy spread (δ s/ s ≈ 0.13%) vs. lepton momentum resolution (σ p T /p T ); (b) W/Z hadronic dijet separation requiring jet energy √ resolution σ E /E ≈ 3–4% (30%/ E); (c) resonant depolarization energy calibration (δm Z ∼ 0.1 MeV) and small-angle Bhabha luminometry (δL/L ∼ 10 −4 ); and (d) flavour-tagging requirements for R b , R c , R s and H → bb̄, cc̄, gg, ss̄. + − → Z(µ + µ − )H recoil-mass simulator incorporating ISR,
deliverables.lab: Stage 1: Python notebook implementing a fast analytical/Monte Carlo e e beamstrahlung, beam energy spread, and parameterized tracker resolution to compute δm H and δσ ZH /σ ZH as functions of σ p T /p 2 T . Stage 2: Load official FCC-ee EDM4hep ZH and ZZ Monte Carlo samples in FCCAnalyses via RDataFrame , apply kinematic selections, and reproduce the recoil-mass spectrum. √
deliverables.problemSet: 4 problems: (1) propagate tracker momentum resolution and beam energy spread into the recoil-mass width σ(m recoil ) at s = 240 GeV and determine the point of diminishing returns; (2) derive the dijet mass separation significance as a function of stochastic resolution a in Z/W √ σ E /E = a/ E ⊕ b; (3) compute the statistical precision on R b , R c , and R s from a √ 3-flavour tagging efficiency/mistag matrix using the Asimov Hessian; (4) estimate the HH → bb̄γγ yield and δλ HHH /λ HHH scaling at FCC-hh ( s = 100 TeV, 20 ab −1 ). Exit criterion: recoil-mass width and R b /R c /R s covariance match published FCC-ee benchmarks within 10%.

dependencies.raw: Prerequisites: Part 7 (Silicon Trackers & Sampling Calorimeters), Part 9 (Particle Flow & PandoraPFA), Lecture 13.1. Downstream: Lectures 13.6 (Trade-off studies) and 13.7 (CLD PF performance capstone).

lectures.abstract: Adapted from the CLIC detector ( CLICdet ) to the continuous-beam, 2 T solenoid, and crab-waist interaction region of FCC-ee, the CLIC-Like Detector (CLD) serves as the mature, full-simulation benchmark for Particle Flow (PF) calorimetry. This lecture examines CLD’s architectural pillars: a three- double-layer monolithic active pixel silicon (MAPS) vertex detector, an all-silicon outer tracker with conformal tracking, a 40-layer silicon-tungsten ( SiW ) ECAL (5 × 5 mm 2 cells, 22 X 0 ), a 44-layer scintillator-steel ( AHCAL ) HCAL (30 × 30 mm 2 tiles, 5.5 λ I ) situated inside the 2 T superconducting solenoid, and an RPC muon system. We analyze how beam-induced backgrounds (incoherent e + e − pairs and synchrotron radiation) constrain the vertex layout and quantify CLD’s jet energy resolution under PandoraPFA and emerging transformer-based global reconstruction.

deliverables.lectureNote: Technical derivations of (a) multiple Coulomb scattering and hit-resolution contributions to CLD’s all-silicon tracker σ(p T )/p 2 T and transverse impact parameter σ(d 0 ) = a ⊕ b/(p sin 3/2 θ); (b) Molière radius (R M ≈ 9 mm in tungsten) vs. cell pitch in the SiW ECAL for two-shower separation in τ → π ± π 0 ν and jet cores; (c) the Particle Flow jet energy resolution budget σ jet 2 = σ 2 + σ 2 2 2 ECAL + σ HCAL + σ confusion ; and (d) conformal trk tracking and software compensation in PandoraPFA . 2 and σ(d ) vs. p and θ using
deliverables.lab: Stage 1: Python simulation of CLD’s 6-layer vertex + 6-layer silicon tracker radial geometry computing σ(p T )/p 0 T T the Gluckstern/Billoir covariance formalism, including material-budget variations (∆X/X 0 ). Stage 2: Load the production CLD_o2_v07 compact geometry from k4geo inside Key4hep / DD4hep , inspect material scans (X 0 and λ I vs. cos θ), and run PandoraPFA on single-pion and Z → q q̄ events in EDM4hep .
deliverables.problemSet: 4 problems: (1) calculate the material budget X/X 0 of CLD’s double-layer vertex barrel and its impact on d 0 resolution at p T = 1 GeV vs. 50 GeV; (2) compute the SiW ECAL sampling fraction and stochastic energy resolution for 40 layers of 1.9 mm W and 0.5 mm Si; (3) decompose of B-field (2 T vs. 3 T) and ECAL inner radius R ECAL ; (4) benchmark PandoraPFA jet energy resolution the PF confusion term σ confusion as a function √ RMS 90 /mean 90 on Z → uds events at s = 91.2 and 365 GeV. Exit criterion: material scan and RMS 90 jet energy resolution reproduce Bacchetta et al. (2019) within 10%.

lectures.abstract: The Innovative Detector for Electron-positron Accelerators (IDEA) is purpose-built for the low-background, precision-dominated environment of FCC-ee. This lecture analyzes IDEA’s distinctive sub-detector synergy: a silicon vertex detector surrounded by an ultra-light, stereo-wire helium-isobutane (90% He / 10% iC 4 H 10 ) drift chamber ( DCH , ∼ 1.6% X 0 at 90 ◦ , 112 layers) offering superior low-p T momentum resolution and particle identification via primary ionization cluster counting (dN/dx), enclosed by a silicon wrapper, a high-resolution dual-readout crystal ECAL, an ultra-thin superconducting solenoid (2 T, ∼ 0.7 X 0 ), and a monolithic SiPM-readout dual-readout fiber calorimeter ( DRCalo ) measuring scintillation (S) and Cherenkov (C) light simultaneously to eliminate event-by-event f em fluctuations.

deliverables.lectureNote: Rigorous derivations of (a) Poissonian cluster-counting (dN/dx) statistics vs. Landau-tail-limited dE/dx energy loss, proving the ∼ 2× improvement in π/K separation power across 2–30 GeV; (b) the dual-readout energy reconstruction equations S = E[f em + (h/e) S (1 − f em )] and C = E[f em + (h/e) C (1 − f em )], solving for E = (S − χC)/(1 − χ) where χ = [1 − (h/e) S ]/[1 − (h/e) C ]; (c) hybrid dual-readout crystal ECAL + fiber HCAL longitudinal calibration; and (d) impact of the ultra-light DCH + thin solenoid on H → γγ, B-physics, and strange-quark jet tagging (s-tagging).
deliverables.lab: Stage 1: Python simulation implementing (i) a Garfield++ -inspired primary-cluster arrival-time generator comparing dN/dx peak-finding vs. truncated-mean dE/dx for K/π separation, and (ii) a dual-readout (S, C) hadronic shower simulator demonstrating linear compensation and elimination of the constant term in σ E /E. Stage 2: Inspect the IDEA_o2_v01 geometry in k4geo ( DD4hep ) and run a Delphes /Key4hep IDEA jet-flavour tagging study ( b , c , s , g separation with and without dN/dx PID).
deliverables.problemSet: 4 problems: (1) derive the χ-parameter and propagate SiPM photoelectron shot noise in S and C into the hadronic stochastic and constant resolution terms; (2) compute the multiple-scattering floor of the IDEA DCH (1.6% X 0 ) vs. CLD’s silicon tracker for 5 GeV and 45 GeV muons; (3) calculate the K/π separation significance S Kπ from dN/dx over a 1.6 m track in 90:10 He/iC 4 H 10 accounting for cluster merging at finite electronics bandwidth; (4) quantify the gain in H → ss̄ sensitivity when adding dN/dx kaon identification to vertex-based flavour tagging. Exit criterion: dual-readout linearity within 1% across 10–100 GeV and dN/dx resolution gain ≥ 1.8× over dE/dx.

(2022) cluster counting, RD52/DREAM dual-readout foundations (2013, 2023); Advanced/optional: 2025/2026 beam-test cluster-counting papers, LSTM cluster-counting algorithms, high-granularity SiPM DRCalo prototypes, and FCC-ee jet-flavour tagging studies.

lectures.abstract: ALLEGRO (A Lepton coLlider Experiment with Granular calorimetRy Read-Out) anchors a general-purpose FCC-ee detector around an inclined-plate, high-granularity noble-liquid electromagnetic calorimeter (lead/tungsten absorbers with liquid argon, LAr, or liquid krypton, LKr), paired with a silicon vertex detector, an ultra-light drift chamber (or silicon tracker), a scintillating-tile HCAL, and a shared-cryostat 2 T solenoid. Inheriting the intrinsic linearity, uniformity, and calibration stability of ATLAS LAr while introducing multilayer PCB readout electrodes with ∼ 11 longitudinal compartments √ and fine transverse segmentation, ALLEGRO targets σ E /E ≈ 8–10%/ E ⊕ 0.7% for photons/electrons alongside full 4D imaging. This lecture covers LAr ionization drift physics, PCB electrode capacitance and noise optimization, and why high-granularity noble-liquid calorimeters are a natural testbed for density clustering ( CLUE ), Graph Neural Network Particle Flow ( MLPF ), and point-cloud generative fast simulation.

deliverables.lectureNote: Analytical treatment of (a) electron drift velocity v d (E), triangular ionization current pulses I(t) = (Q 0 /t d )(1 − t/t d ), and bipolar CR-RC n pulse shaping; (b) series thermal vs. parallel noise scaling with PCB readout pad capacitance C d and shaping time τ s ; (c) inclined-plate geometry (50 ◦ inclination) eliminating azimuthal cracks while maintaining uniform sampling fraction across ϕ; and (d) formulation of 3D topological clustering ( CLUE ), MLPF graph-based particle reconstruction, and sliding-window/DNN hadron calibration.
deliverables.lab: Stage 1: Python notebook modeling the LAr triangular drift pulse, CR-RC shaper transfer function, electronic noise vs. cell capacitance C d , 2 and a lightweight PyTorch GNN/attention prototype mapping 3D calorimeter hit clouds + tracks to reconstructed particle candidates. Stage 2: Load ALLEGRO_o2_v01 from k4geo in Key4hep , inspect the 11-layer inclined LAr ECAL segmentation, run CLUE clustering on simulated photon/π 0 showers, and compare π 0 → γγ separation against a sliding-window baseline.
deliverables.problemSet: 4 problems: (1) derive the optimal shaping time τ opt minimizing total equivalent noise charge (ENC) for a given LAr cell capacitance C d and preamplifier noise spectral density; (2) compute the sampling fraction and stochastic energy resolution for inclined Pb/LAr vs. W/LAr and Pb/LKr configurations; (3) implement CLUE ’s local-density (ρ i ) and nearest-higher-density (δ i ) clustering metrics on a 2D synthetic shower overlap and analyze complexity scaling O(N ); (4) evaluate single-π − energy resolution improvement from DNN 4D shower weighting vs. fixed-window benchmark calibration. Exit criterion: LAr pulse shaper reproduces expected signal-to-noise peak within 5%, and CLUE separates overlapping π 0 → γγ clusters down to ∆R ∼ 2 cell widths.

lectures.abstract: L dt ≈ 20 ab −1 ) represents an order-of-magnitude Transitioning from FCC-ee to the 100 TeV proton-proton FCC-hh (L peak = 3 × 10 35 cm −2 s −1 , R leap in both energy and experimental harshness. This lecture dissects the FCC-hh reference detector: a 4 T central solenoid flanked by forward dipoles (or twin solenoids), extended tracking and calorimetry out to |η| = 6 to capture forward vector-boson fusion jets, a 10.5 λ I LAr + scintillating-tile calorimeter system containing multi-TeV showers, and 30 ps 4D timing layers. We quantify the extreme radiation fluences (up to ∼ 10 17 n eq cm −2 in the inner tracker and forward calorimeters), ultraboosted W/Z/H/t jet collimation (∆R ∼ 2m/p T ≪ 0.1), and pileup mitigation at ⟨µ⟩ ∼ 1000 via PUPPI , SoftKiller , LGAD timing, and graph neural networks.

deliverables.lectureNote: Quantitative derivations of (a) inelastic pp cross-section scaling (σ inel ≈ 108 mb at 100 TeV) yielding ⟨µ⟩ = Lσ inel /ν BC ≈ 1000 simultaneous interactions per 25 ns bunch crossing; (b) 4D vertex density in (z, t) space and the pileup rejection factor from σ t ≈ 30 ps LGAD timing layers; (c) radiation-damage scaling (NIEL Φ eq and TID) with pseudorapidity η and radial distance r; (d) longitudinal shower containment scaling (L 98% ∝ ln E) requiring > 10.5 λ I HCAL depth; and (e) mathematical formulation of PUPPI local shape variable α i and SoftKiller dynamic p cut T .
deliverables.lab: Stage 1: Python simulation generating synthetic hard-scatter dijet/HH events overlaid with µ ∈ {50, 200, 1000} minimum-bias pileup vertices in (z, t) space, implementing and comparing Charged Hadron Subtraction (CHS), SoftKiller , PUPPI , and 4D time-windowed PUPPI on jet p T resolution and mass resolution. Stage 2: Run the FCC-hh reference detector card in Delphes + FCCAnalyses on simulated pp → HH → bb̄γγ and multi-TeV boosted Z ′ → tt̄ samples, evaluating pileup and granularity impacts.
deliverables.problemSet: 4 problems: (1) compute the longitudinal vertex overlap probability for ⟨µ⟩ = 1000 (σ z = 5 cm, σ t = 180 ps) with and without a 30 ps timing detector; (2) calculate the decay-product opening angle ∆R of a 5 TeV W boson and a 10 TeV top quark and derive the required ECAL/HCAL transverse cell granularity (∆η × ∆ϕ); (3) prove the scaling of SoftKiller runtime O(N ) vs. jet-area subtraction and analyze its bias on soft radiation inside signal jets; (4) compute the integrated 1 MeV neutron-equivalent fluence at r = 2.5 cm and at |η| = 5.5 (r = 8 cm, z = 16.6 m) for 20 ab −1 . Exit criterion: Stage 1 4D- PUPPI reduces jet p T RMS at µ = 1000 by ≥ 40% relative to CHS alone.

lectures.abstract: Real collider detectors are never unconstrained optima; they are engineered compromises across physics reach, Machine-Detector Interface (MDI) constraints, technology readiness, and cost. This lecture formalizes systems-level detector optimization for FCC-ee across four interacting axes: (1) solenoid field (2 T cap at the Z pole to avoid emittance blow-up from the 30 mrad crossing angle vs. 3 T at ZH); (2) tracker architecture (all-silicon CLD vs. gaseous DCH IDEA/ALLEGRO, material budget vs. hit precision); (3) calorimetry paradigm (PF-driven SiW + AHCAL vs. dual-readout crystal/fiber vs. granular LAr); and (4) vertexing and PID (dN/dx vs. dedicated RICH/TOF layers) for b/c/s/g jet flavour tagging. Students learn to construct Fisher-information sensitivity gradients ∂σ obs /∂θ det and Pareto frontiers mapping detector parameter sweeps directly onto Higgs, EW, and flavour precision.

deliverables.lectureNote: Formal treatment of (a) the MDI crossing-angle emittance constraint ∆ϵ y ∝ B z 2 L sol θ c 2 restricting FCC-ee Z-pole solenoid fields to 2 T; (b) multi-objective Pareto optimization over (σ p T /p 2 T , σ d 0 , σ E /E, PID, Cost); (c) differentiable/surrogate detector optimization concepts connecting DD4hep geometry parameters to downstream physics figures of merit; and (d) comparative scorecard across CLD, IDEA, and ALLEGRO aligned with the ECFA Detector R&D Roadmap DRD collaborations (DRD1–DRD8).
deliverables.lab: Stage 1: Python multi-objective trade-off studio sweeping solenoid field B ∈ [1.5, 3.0] T, inner beampipe radius r bp ∈ [10, 15] mm, tracker X/X 0 , and calorimeter stochastic term a ∈ [15%, 50%] to compute Pareto fronts for (δm H , δσ ZH , δBR(H → ss̄), Solenoid+Calo Cost). Stage 2: Execute a parameterized Delphes card sweep inside FCCAnalyses comparing CLD, IDEA, and ALLEGRO cards on e + e − → Z(µ + µ − )H(bb̄/cc̄/ss̄) and W W → q q̄q q̄ benchmarks.
deliverables.problemSet: 4 problems: (1) derive the vertical emittance growth from a 2 T vs. 3 T detector solenoid with compensating anti-solenoids at √ s = 91.2 GeV and 240 GeV; (2) compute the marginal sensitivity ∂(δm H )/∂(σ p T /p 2 T ) and identify the exact crossover where beam energy spread dominates over tracker resolution; (3) evaluate the impact of inner vertex radius (10 mm vs. 15 mm) and material budget (0.1% vs. 0.3% X 0 /layer) on c- and s-jet tagging ROC curves; (4) draft a 2-page quantitative trade-off memo selecting an integrated four-IP FCC-ee detector portfolio (balancing complementarity across CLD, IDEA, and ALLEGRO). Exit criterion: Pareto frontier reproduces published 2 T vs. 3 T and r bp sensitivity trends within 10%.

lectures.abstract: Lecture 13.7 is the integrative studio of Part 13, bridging self-built pedagogical prototypes with production FCC software workflows through three end-to-end capstone projects. In Capstone A, students architect a complete, modular Python toy Particle Flow engine (helix track propagation, 3D topological calorimeter clustering, track–cluster χ 2 linking, split/merge confusion diagnostics, and anti-k T jet reconstruction) and benchmark it against truth particles. In Capstone B, students execute a full FCCAnalyses ( RDataFrame ) physics analysis on EDM4hep samples (e.g., e + e − → Z(ℓ + ℓ − )H cross-section/invisible-decay search) and construct a serialized JSON pyhf HistFactory statistical model with systematic nuisance parameters to extract profile-likelihood confidence intervals and CL s limits. In Capstone C, students perform a full-simulation CLD Particle Flow performance study ( k4geo + DD4hep + PandoraPFA / MLPF ) evaluating RMS 90 jet energy resolution, angular resolution, and confusion breakdowns across jet energies.

deliverables.lectureNote: Architecture blueprint and validation protocol for all three capstones: (a) mathematical specification of helix–calorimeter surface intersection, Mahalanobis track–cluster matching, and RMS 90 robust resolution estimators; (b) FCCAnalyses two-stage ( stage1 skimmer → stage2 histogrammer → pyhf workspace) workflow design; (c) HistFactory likelihood construction L(µ, θ) with Barlow–Beeston MC statistical uncertainties and asymptotic profile-likelihood test statistics q̃ µ (Cowan et al. 2011); and (d) full-simulation CLD performance audit checklist.
deliverables.lab: Three structured project tracks with automated CI verification: Capstone A (Stage 1 Python) builds a pure-Python/NumPy/SciPy toy PF engine tested on 10,000 synthetic multi-particle jets outputting energy response, linearity, RMS 90 resolution, and confusion breakdown; Capstone B (Stage 2 FCCAnalyses + pyhf ) builds a reproducible FCCAnalyses pipeline on EDM4hep MC samples exporting binned templates to a pyhf JSON workspace with pull plots, nuisance-parameter impact rankings, and 95% CL CL s exclusion limits; Capstone C (Stage 2 Key4hep /CLD) executes a full-simulation CLD ( CLD_o2_v07 ) PandoraPFA (and optional MLPF ) study evaluating single-particle and Z → uds dijet performance across E jet ∈ [45, 180] GeV and | cos θ| < 0.9.
deliverables.problemSet: Capstone defense rubric and validation suite: (1) unit-test suite for Capstone A verifying 4-momentum conservation, track–cluster matching efficiency > 95% for isolated pions, and ≥ 30% jet resolution gain over calorimeter-only reconstruction; (2) statistical validation of Capstone B verifying Asimov expected limits, pulls within ±1σ, and exact reproducibility of the pyhf JSON workspace; (3) quantitative comparison in Capstone C of CLD PandoraPFA jet energy resolution against Bacchetta et al. (2019). Exit criterion: all three capstone repositories pass automated tests and produce publication-ready figures and a 10-page technical summary.

parts.abstract: Technical mastery alone does not make an effective experimental or phenomenological particle physicist; modern high-energy physics operates through global, multi-thousand-author collaborations governed by rigorous internal review, strict documentation standards, and open-science mandates. Part 14 equips students with the professional operating system of HEP research across three progressive lectures: critically reading arXiv literature and authoring structured analysis notes and talks (14.1); navigating large-collaboration governance, editorial boards, CI-backed documentation, and software stewardship (14.2); and upholding research ethics, FAIR data management, containerized analysis preservation ( REANA / HEPData / Rivet ), and transparent authorship credit under CERN, COPE, ALLEA, and DORA standards (14.3).

deliverables.lectureNote: Concise, actionable graduate handbook (~75 pages across Lectures 14.1–14.3) featuring annotated HEP paper anatomy, internal analysis note (ANA/INT) templates, figure-design standards, collaboration review-cycle flowcharts (Phase 0 → Editorial Board → Collaboration-Wide Review → arXiv/SCOAP3), FAIR metadata checklists, and real-world case studies in authorship, data preservation, and statistical blinding.
deliverables.lab: Two-stage professional-practice labs: Stage 1 builds personal Python/LaTeX/Git tooling (INSPIRE-HEP/arXiv API literature-triage scripts, automated BibTeX/DOI verification, structured analysis-note LaTeX skeleton, and local REANA YAML workflow packaging); Stage 2 integrates directly with HEP community infrastructure ( HEPData YAML submission validation, pyhf likelihood archival, GitLab CI LaTeX/figure build pipelines modeled on ATLAS FENCE , and REANA / Rivet containerized re-execution).

Exit criterion: zero broken citations/LaTeX CI errors, validated HEPData YAML schema, and bit-for-bit reproducible container execution of a pyhf limit.

lectures.abstract: Effective scientific communication is an analytical discipline, not an afterthought. This lecture teaches a structured, three-pass protocol for reading hep-ex , hep-ph , and physics.ins-det papers on arXiv and tracing citation networks, conference records, and data tables via INSPIRE-HEP and HEPData . Students then master the distinct genres of HEP writing: the exhaustive internal analysis note (INT/ANA) designed for reproducibility and Editorial Board scrutiny versus the tight, narrative-driven journal manuscript (JHEP, EPJC, PRD, PRL) formatted under arXiv and SCOAP3 standards. We conclude with quantitative visual design (colorblind-safe palettes, ratio/pull panels, uncertainty-band conventions) and structuring crisp 12-minute parallel-session conference talks with defensive backup slides.

deliverables.lectureNote: Detailed guide covering (a) the 3-pass paper-reading algorithm and six diagnostic questions (Carey et al. 2020); (b) INSPIRE-HEP query syntax ( a , t , cn , citedby , BibTeX export) and arXiv versioning/endorsement workflows; (c) structural anatomy of a HEP internal analysis note (Data/MC samples, Object Definitions, Event Selection, Background Estimation, Systematic Uncertainties, Statistical Model, Blinding/Unblinding Checklist) vs. a journal paper (Context–Content–Conclusion structure, Mensh & Kording 2017); and (d) plot-style and conference-talk engineering.
deliverables.lab: Stage 1: Python script querying the INSPIRE-HEP REST API to build a structured reading digest and verified BibTeX file for a chosen FCC-ee benchmark channel, paired with a matplotlib / mplhep figure-style audit script enforcing readable typography, ratio panels, and uncertainty bands. Stage 2: Convert Capstone B ( FCCAnalyses + pyhf ) into a complete, LaTeX-compiled internal analysis note ( INT style) and a 12-slide Beamer conference presentation with backup slides.
deliverables.problemSet: 4 tasks: (1) write a 1.5-page structured referee report on a recent hep-ex FCC-ee or LHC preprint evaluating statistical methodology, systematic completeness, and figure clarity; (2) refactor a dense, poorly structured 400-word draft abstract and introduction using Context–Content– √ Conclusion rules; (3) audit and regenerate 3 plots from Part 13 to satisfy HEP publication standards (luminosity/ s labels, ratio pads, error-bar transparency); (4) deliver a timed 12-minute practice talk + 3-minute Q&A defense. Exit criterion: LaTeX note compiles with zero warnings, all references verified against INSPIRE-HEP DOIs/arXiv IDs, and referee report addresses all 6 methodological criteria.

lectures.abstract: Modern collider experiments—from ATLAS and CMS to future FCC-ee detector collaborations and CERN-hosted DRD consortia—coordinate thousands of physicists across hundreds of institutes over multi-decade lifecycles. This lecture demystifies how large collaborations actually function: institutional governance (Collaboration Board, Spokesperson, Physics/Detector Coordinators, Resource Coordinators), qualification tasks and operational service work, and the multi-stage internal publication review pipeline (Analysis Registration/Phase 0, Editorial Board formation, blind unblinding sign-off, Circulation 1 & 2, and Publication Committee approval). We emphasize modern documentation culture: GitLab CI-automated LaTeX and analysis validation (modeled on ATLAS FENCE ), software stewardship principles from the HEP Software Foundation (HSF), and effective meeting/Indico project management.

deliverables.lectureNote: Operational playbook detailing (a) anatomy of a large HEP collaboration organigram and decision-making bodies; (b) complete lifecycle of a physics result from Phase 0 registration through EdBoard review, blinding/unblinding gates, and journal submission; (c) engineering a zero-friction documentation culture (living READMEs, versioned k4geo /analysis configs, CI pipelines for LaTeX/linting/unit tests, and Indico agenda hygiene); and (d) managing cross-timezone collaborative software and hardware milestones using issue trackers and merge-request reviews.

Stage 2: Conduct a structured mock Editorial Board (EdBoard) review using merge requests and issue threads on a peer’s FCCAnalyses + pyhf repository, enforcing a formal blinding-to-unblinding checklist modeled on ATLAS FENCE pipelines.

lectures.abstract: Publicly funded mega-science facilities like the LHC and FCC carry an explicit covenant with society: data, software, and statistical results must be trustworthy, preserved, and reusable decades after collection. This closing lecture examines the three pillars of responsible HEP research. First, Data Policy & FAIR Stewardship: the DPHEP four-level data classification, the 2020 CERN Open Data Policy ( CERN-OPEN-2020-013 ), the 2022 CERN Open Science Policy, and the FAIR principles (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable). Second, Computational Reproducibility & Reinterpretation: publishing digitized tables and full pyhf JSON likelihoods on HEPData , particle-level routines in Rivet , and containerized declarative workflows on REANA . Third, Research Integrity & Credit: preventing confirmation bias via blinding, adhering to COPE and ALLEA (2023) ethics codes (including AI-tool disclosure), and navigating authorship and career recognition across alphabetical megacollaborations, CRediT contributor taxonomies, and DORA assessment reforms.

deliverables.lectureNote: Rigorous synthesis of (a) DPHEP Levels 1–4 data preservation and CERN’s 5-year embargo / CC0 release model for Level 3 reconstructed data; (b) FAIR compliance checklist for HEP digital objects (persistent DOIs, EDM4hep / HEPData YAML schemas, open licenses); (c) architecture of containerized analysis preservation ( Docker / Apptainer + reana.yaml + pyhf JSON + Rivet / Contur ); and (d) ethical decision frameworks from COPE and ALLEA (2023) covering data fabrication/falsification, p-hacking/look-elsewhere abuse, authorship disputes, CRediT roles, DORA principles, and generative-AI disclosure rules.
deliverables.lab: Stage 1: Package the Capstone B pyhf analysis into a fully self-contained, FAIR-compliant archive: generate a validated HEPData YAML submission ( submission.yaml + digitized tables + pyhf JSON likelihood), write a reana.yaml declarative workflow specification with pinned container image, and verify bit-for-bit reproducibility of the limit plot. Stage 2: Execute a containerized REANA (or local reana-client /Docker) re-run of an open-data/recast workflow and draft a Zenodo/CERN Open Data metadata record plus CRediT contributor statement.
deliverables.problemSet: 4 tasks: (1) classify 8 concrete FCC/LHC data products into DPHEP Levels 1–4 and design a 20-year FAIR data-management plan (DMP) for a new FCC-ee detector concept; (2) write a HEPData YAML table and pyhf likelihood patch for a two-channel search and validate it against the hepdata-validator schema; (3) analyze three realistic HEP ethics case studies (premature unblinding / post-hoc cut tuning; dispute over standing alphabetical authorship vs. early-career software credit; undisclosed LLM generation of analysis code/text) citing exact COPE and ALLEA (2023) clauses; (4) propose a concrete career-evaluation dossier aligned with DORA and CRediT for a PhD candidate whose primary contribution is Key4hep reconstruction software rather than a standalone physics paper. Exit criterion: HEPData YAML passes schema validation, reana.yaml reproduces numerical outputs within 10 −6 , and ethics analyses cite verified policy clauses.

learningOutcomes: Distinguish DPHEP Levels 1–4 experimental data products and explain
the embargo, licensing (CC0), and metadata provisions of the CERN Open Data and Open Science Policies.
Evaluate datasets, likelihoods, and analysis repositories against each of the four FAIR guiding principles.

Construct and validate a HEPData YAML submission containing digitized measurements, covariance matrices, and serialized pyhf JSON statistical models. Author a declarative, containerized reana.yaml workflow enabling
long-term computational reproducibility and BSM reinterpretation.
Identify and mitigate subtle research-integrity hazards in HEP, including post-unblinding bias, selective reporting, and improper use of AI tools under COPE and ALLEA (2023) standards.
Articulate how megacollaboration alphabetical authorship interacts with CRediT contributor taxonomies and DORA responsible research assessment.
